report: Chronic facial ulcers, sicca, Raynaud, arthralgia, dysphagia, ANA 1:360, low C4, and orbital granulomatous inflammation support autoimmune disease. Negative ANCA/cultures and benign biopsy argue against infection/malignancy; polarizable material suggests foreign-body reaction, but no exposure. Elevated ACE and granulomas raise sarcoidosis. Sjögren syndrome with systemic features is the leading refined hypothesis, though missing anti-Ro/La, RF, Schirmer/salivary flow, chest CT prevent confirmation.
